html:
The battle of 1 March 1896 near the town of Adwa in northern Ethiopia, where the army of Emperor Menelik II destroyed an Italian invasion force. It was the greatest defeat of a European army in Africa in the age of colonial conquest.

Italy held Eritrea and claimed, under the Treaty of Wuchale, that Ethiopia was its protectorate. Menelik rejected this and gathered a large army armed with modern rifles. Empress Taytu Betul led her own troops. The Italian commander, General Oreste Baratieri, attacked with a much smaller force split into columns that lost touch in the mountains, and they were beaten one by one. Thousands of Italians were killed and many taken prisoner.

The Treaty of Addis Ababa that October recognised Ethiopia's full independence. In Italy the defeat brought down the government of Francesco Crispi. Across Africa and its diaspora Adwa became a symbol of resistance and of Pan-Africanism. Italy took its revenge in the invasion of 1935.
